The congregation had been dissolved by the Archdiocese before the petition was filed
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: Credible material established that the daughters were being confined and their signed statements were extracted under threat. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not an essential element to establish liability for negligence?
options: Existence of a legal duty to take care
Breach of that duty by failure to act as a reasonable person
Actual damage suffered by the plaintiff
Existence of a wrongful intention to cause harm
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: Existence of a wrongful intention to cause harm. Accordingly, option D is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
If a court finds that a pre-contractual statement is a mere representation rather than a
binding term, upon what factor might the available legal remedy depend?
options: Whether the misstatement was made fraudulently, negligently, or innocently.
Whether the statement was an obvious opinion intended to induce the sale.
Whether a reasonable person would have understood it to allocate legal risk.
Whether the statement was formally reduced into the final written contract.
questions.solution: the passage explicitly lists fraud, negligence, and innocence as the dependencies for determining the remedy of a mere representation.

questions.questionText:
What is the specific intent required for an act to be considered genocide under international
law?
options: Intent to gain political power
Intent to cause widespread harm
Intent to destroy a protected group
Intent to achieve economic interests
questions.solution: Under the United Nations Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, genocide requires a deliberate intention to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group. This special intent is what differentiates genocide from other international crimes.

questions.questionText:

Procedure established by law meant only a legislatively enacted procedure
Article 21 automatically included the right to dignity
Articles 14, 19, and 21 were read together

questions.questionText:
According to Home Minister G. Parameshwara, why were existing "preventive restrictions"

Temporary bans on inflammatory speech were not a long-term solution to the recurring link
between speech and violent incidents.

The Supreme Court had ruled that all existing state laws on communal hate were
unconstitutional.
Existing laws only focused on the victim rather than the offender.

questions.questionText:
The author's invocation of Fiat justitia ruat caelum in the passage primarily underscores

judicial decisions must align with the emotional pulse of the citizenry to sustain democratic

adherence to justice must remain unwavering even if such adherence unsettles political or

courts must occasionally suspend the rule of law to protect constitutional harmony and
prevent institutional friction

the maxim is symbolic of judicial restraint rather than intervention in matters involving
political or social controversy
questions.solution: The passage states that Fiat justitia ruat caelum "epitomises the judiciary's unflinching commitment to the rule of law, even when such fidelity provokes institutional disquiet or political reprisal" and that "justice, anchored in constitutional principle, must be rendered irrespective of political tempests or societal disquietude." This directly supports option (B)—justice must prevail regardless of the unsettling consequences. Option (A) contradicts the passage's emphasis on constitutional mor

questions.questionText:

Valid contract with no available remedy.
Void contract due to lack of consideration.
Voidable contract due to misrepresentation.

questions.questionText:
Arjun fears that his joint venture partner will sell off machinery crucial to an upcoming
arbitration. What remedy is available to Arjun under the Act?
options: File a police complaint.
File a challenge under Section 34.
Approach the court under Section 9 for a temporary injunction.
Wait for arbitration to start.
questions.solution: The passage clearly states that Section 9 allows parties to approach courts for interim relief before, during, or after arbitral proceedings, but before enforcement of the award. Such interim relief includes temporary injunctions and preservation of assets.

questions.questionText:
What was the Supreme Court's direction regarding the panel of names for tribunal
           appointments to curb excessive executive discretion?
options: That the panel should include both advocates and civil servants.
That the panel should be selected by the Prime Minister.
That the government should propose three names per vacancy.

That only one name per post must be recommended by the Search-cum-Selection
Committee.

questions.questionText:
Suppose the CCI cannot determine Apple’s relevant turnover for the Indian segment of
     the App Store. According to the passage, what is the most appropriate regulatory
     response?
options: The CCI must drop the penalty because relevant turnover is essential.
The CCI must estimate a minimum turnover using developer surveys.
The CCI may use Apple’s global turnover to calculate penalties.
The CCI can impose only a symbolic penalty of ₹1 crore.

questions.questionText:
The State enacts a surveillance law to monitor online communications to prevent cybercrime. A
civil liberties group challenges the law, claiming it disproportionately infringes on citizens’ right to
privacy. The court must evaluate whether less restrictive measures could achieve the same
objective without violating fundamental rights. Which aspect of proportionality is the court
primarily examining?
options: Legitimacy, checking if the law serves a proper public purpose.
Suitability, assessing whether surveillance can technically detect cybercrime.
Deference, giving absolute authority to the legislature in policy matters.
Necessity, determining if no less restrictive alternative exists to achieve objectives.
questions.solution: Option (a): Incorrect. While legitimacy matters, the challenge focuses on alternative measures. Option (b): Incorrect. Suitability assesses capability, not comparative restrictiveness. Option (c): Incorrect. Deference limits intervention but does not decide proportionality itself. Option (d): Correct. Necessity tests whether the State could achieve its aim using less restrictive means.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements about the EIA process is most accurate based on the
passage?
options:
The EIA report is prepared solely by government-appointed independent consultants to
ensure objectivity.

The credibility of EIA reports is strengthened by the fact that they are funded by project
proponents themselves.

Enforcement gaps, proponent-funded assessments, copy-paste reporting, and weak
accountability mechanisms have led to credibility problems in several cases.

Once environmental clearance is granted, no further monitoring or compliance verification
is required.
questions.solution: The passage explicitly identifies that enforcement gaps, proponent-funded assessments, copy-paste reporting, and weak accountability mechanisms have led to credibility problems. Option C accurately reflects this.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following is NOT cited as a rationale or potential benefit of implementing
        simultaneous elections ('One Nation, One Election')?
options: Reducing the massive financial burden associated with conducting separate elections.

Ensuring the relevance of regional parties by preventing state issues from being

Eliminating the need for the Election Commission of India.

Preventing policy paralysis by reducing the frequency of the Model Code of Conduct being

questions.questionText: P and Q secretly agreed to illegally divert government relief funds into private accounts. Before any transfer occurred, Q rented an office and created false financial records intended to conceal the scheme. Which option best applies?
options: Only preparation exists because conspiracy requires completion of the offence.
Conspiracy may exist because there was agreement followed by acts in furtherance of the plan.
Conspiracy does not exist because the funds were never actually diverted.
Conspiracy cannot exist where financial offences are involved.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: Conspiracy may exist because there was agreement followed by acts in furtherance of the plan. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following Supreme Court decisions is regarded as having laid the foundation for
the development of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India by significantly liberalising the
traditional rule of locus standi and allowing public-spirited individuals to approach the court
on behalf of others?
options: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India
ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India. Accordingly, option A is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Under Article 19, the State is empowered to impose "reasonable restrictions" on freedoms. These
restrictions must be aimed at preserving:
options: The financial profit of the State.
The popularity of the ruling government.
Sovereignty, integrity, and public order.
The absolute power of the local police.
questions.solution: Article 19(2) allows restrictions on grounds like sovereignty, integrity, security of the state, and public order.

questions.questionText:

options: Financial power to levy and collect taxes and land revenue

questions.questionText:

legal status in Berubari Union?
options: The Preamble was merely symbolic and politically motivated
The Preamble lacked enforceable & operative provisions.
The Preamble contradicted the federal structure
The Preamble was amendable only by referendum
questions.solution: As mentioned in the passage, the Court held that the Preamble has no enforceable or operative provisions and therefore cannot confer powers or impose limitations. Hence, it was denied substantive legal status.

It grants protection only within the class of matrimonial services
It allows protection against misuse even in unrelated classes of goods or services
It automatically entitles the proprietor to punitive damages

questions.questionText:
Vikram borrowed a laptop from his office to complete work at home but instead sold it to a friend.
The company discovered the sale and filed a complaint. Which offence is most relevant?
options: Theft, because the laptop was taken secretly without company consent.
Criminal breach of trust, because property was entrusted but misused dishonestly.
Robbery, because the property was sold for personal gain.
Cheating, because the friend was deceived into buying the laptop.
questions.solution: Option (a): Incorrect. Theft requires secret taking from possession without consent. Option (b): Correct. Misuse of entrusted property constitutes criminal breach of trust. Option (c): Incorrect. Robbery requires immediate use of force. Option (d): Incorrect. Cheating requires inducement of property delivery by deception. Reference: "The act must involve unlawful taking, conversion, or obstruction, depending on the nature of the offence."

questions.questionText:

Employment status depends on the substance of the relationship, not the employer’s

None of the above.

questions.questionText:

options: Article 51-A
The Preamble
Article 44
Articles 29 and 30
questions.solution: The passage explicitly states that through the Preamble, the people resolved to constitute India into a secular republic. Incorrect Options:

questions.questionText:
The Chief Justice refuses to hear a case against the government citing executive pressure. The
government then transfers him to another court. Lawyers challenge the transfer. Which Dicey

options: None, because transfers of senior judges are treated as internal administrative matters

Equality before law, because the Chief Justice receives special and unusual treatment
Supremacy of law, because the independent judiciary must supervise the executive
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: Predominance of legal spirit, because judicial decisions are being improperly coerced. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Aryan and Kabir are neighbours in an apartment complex. They agree to share the costs and
maintenance of a large water tank on the roof for their mutual benefit. One day, the tank bursts

Aryan sues Kabir for damages under Strict Liability. Which defence can Kabir most effectively
use?
options: Act of God.
Statutory Authority.
Volenti Non-Fit Injuria (Mutual Benefit).
Plaintiff's Own Fault.
questions.solution: The passage states that if a dangerous substance is maintained for the "mutual benefit of both parties," it is a valid defence (Volenti Non-Fit Injuria). Since both neighbours agreed to and benefited from the tank, Kabir is not strictly liable to Aryan.

questions.questionText:

questions.questionText:

questions.solution: Statement 1 — True The passage explicitly identifies employer-employee and principal-agent as core relationships where vicarious liability arises. Statement 2 — False The passage states the opposite — employers are generally not liable for independent contractors.

questions.questionText:

Preparation of a panchnama documenting the search and the items found at the premises.

Prior written intimation to the concerned Magistrate before the search operation is

Providing a copy of the list of seized articles to the occupant of the searched premises.

questions.questionText:

options: No, because the Cricket Association is a private body and not a ‘State’.

questions.solution: Under Article 226, a High Court can issue a writ against any person or authority for the enforcement of any legal right, provided the authority is exercising a public function, as a cricket association does.

questions.questionText: T contracted to sell a rare painting to U. Before delivery, T intentionally destroyed the painting after receiving a better commercial offer from another buyer and argued that the contract had become impossible to perform. Which option is correct?
options: The contract is frustrated because destruction of subject matter creates impossibility.
T is excused because performance became impossible before delivery.
T cannot rely on frustration because the impossibility was self-induced.

questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: T cannot rely on frustration because the impossibility was self-induced. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:

questions.questionText: E, a micro-influencer, receives a free gadget from a company and posts a positive review without disclosing that the product was gifted. The review influences several consumers to purchase the product. What is the correct legal position?
options: The non-disclosure may amount to misleading advertisement as it conceals a material connection.

Liability arises only if the product is defective.
The influencer is exempt due to having a small audience.

questions.questionText: Which of the following situation does not describe a valid defence against negligence?

questions.questionText: A minor enters into a marriage without coercion. Upon attaining majority, the individual chooses to continue the marriage and does not seek annulment. Which statement is most accurate?

The marriage is voidable and becomes effectively valid if not annulled.

questions.questionText:

questions.questionText:

Sustainable development requires prioritising short-term ecological harm over long-

Environmental governance must involve informed balancing rather than categorical

Judicial orders should permanently fix environmental policy choices.

questions.questionText:
Priya sued Dev for recovery of Rs. 5 lakhs as a loan. The District Court held that only Rs. 2 lakhs

Yes, because she has obtained better evidence for the claim

No, but only if Dev submits a formal written legal objection

questions.questionText:
As mandated by the JJ Act, 2015, what is the required composition of a Juvenile

A chairperson from the legal services authority and two child rights activists.

questions.questionText:
The Selection Committee, a quasi-judicial body, begins proceedings to ban KL Rahul based on a

Mandamus, to command them to follow the rules.
Quo Warranto, against the committee members.
questions.solution: When a tribunal is acting or threatening to act in excess of its jurisdiction, Prohibition is issued to prevent it from continuing the proceedings.

questions.questionText:
Raghav filed a suit despite an arbitration clause. The court found the clause valid but still
refused to refer the matter to arbitration, saying it had already spent effort on the suit. Was

options: Yes, courts can retain jurisdiction if they have started hearing.

The passage also emphasizes the principle of minimal judicial intervention under Section 5.

questions.questionText:
What specific requirement does the DPDPA mandate for the processing of children's

options: It requires obtaining verifiable parental consent before processing a child's data.

It delegates the rule-making for children's data entirely to the individual state

It completely bans the processing of any personal data belonging to children below
the age of 18.

questions.questionText:
The suggested measure to enact anti-SLAPP legislation is designed to address a

questions.questionText: A foreign naval vessel passes through the territorial waters of State X while conducting live weapons drills. State X protests. Which is the most appropriate legal position?

The vessel is entitled to innocent passage regardless of its activities within territorial waters.
The vessel has full freedom of navigation in all maritime zones including territorial waters.
The activity is permissible as long as no damage is caused to State X.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The activity may render the passage non-innocent as it threatens the security of the coastal state. Accordingly, option A is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:

options: The Prohibition of Money Laundering Act, 2005
The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002
The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2005
The Proceeds of Money Laundering Act, 2002

questions.questionText:
Based on the passage, if a person is accused of a crime that took place on May 20, 2024, but the
trial begins in 2025, which law will govern their punishment?
options: Both IPC and BNS, whichever provides a lighter sentence.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), as it is the law in force during the trial.
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), as it governs the trial procedure.
The Indian Penal Code (IPC), because the transition to the new laws is prospective.
questions.solution: The passage explicitly states that the transition is "prospective," meaning crimes committed before July 1, 2024, continue to be tried under the old IPC. questions.questionText:
According to the passage, which of the following is a mandatory legal precondition for a
statement to be admissible under the discovery exception?

The confession of the core crime must be fully recorded by a Magistrate prior to the

The physical fact discovered must be one that was already known to the investigating

The entire statement, including the confession of guilt, must be admitted to provide

The individual must be formally accused of an offense and be in active police custody.
questions.solution: This is correct because the Supreme Court mandates strict preconditions, specifically that the individual must be formally accused and in active police custody.

questions.questionText:
Vikram, a landlord, decided to increase the rent of his tenant, Maya, without providing the legally required

Maya possessed a legal right to receive the statutory notice before a rent increase. Vikram's failure to comply with this legal obligation amounts to an infringement of her legal right. Even if Maya ultimately paid the increased rent, the violation of her legal right itself makes the action actionable, reflecting the principle of Injuria Sine Damnum. Therefore, Option C is correct. Why other options are incorrect: A. This is incorrect because the key issue is the violation of Maya's legal right, not merely the

questions.questionText: A research vessel from State A conducts marine scientific research 250 nautical miles from any coast. State B objects, claiming interference. Which is the best position?
options: State B's objection is valid because all research requires consent of all states.
The activity is unlawful as research is prohibited on the high seas.
The activity is valid only if it benefits all states equally.
The activity is permissible as part of the freedom of the high seas.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The activity is permissible as part of the freedom of the high seas. Accordingly, option D is the keyed legal result.

options:

questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: Universal Declaration of Human Rights on fundamental human freedoms. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:

his neighbour, Priya, who lives downstream. However, Priya is an environmental activist and sues Rohan for

questions.solution: According to the passage, a tort requires the infringement of a legal right vested in the plaintiff. This is incorrect because environmental harm alone does not establish a tort unless the plaintiff's legal rights are infringed.

The 44th Amendment Act
The 73rd Amendment Act
The 101st Amendment Act

questions.questionText:
Industrial machinery creates a constant hum audible throughout a suburb, disturbing
       the peace. A local musician claims the noise destroys their ability to work from home.
       Do they have standing to sue for public nuisance?
options:
No, their harm is the same kind of disturbance as the community's, just more
             severe.
No, noise alone cannot be a public nuisance without a physical obstruction.

Yes, because the harm to their professional work is a special injury different in
              kind.
Yes, because any individual can sue once a public nuisance is established.

questions.questionText:
According to the provisions of the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024,
          what is the stipulated term for the next Lok Sabha if it is dissolved before
          completing its full five-year tenure?
options: It will serve only the unexpired portion of the term of the dissolved House.
Its term will be decided by a resolution of the new Lok Sabha.
It will serve a term fixed by the President, not exceeding five years.
It will serve a fresh five-year term.

questions.questionText:
According to the passage, the "Golden Hour" principle refers to the legal and moral duty of medical
professionals regarding:
options: The right to free legal aid for accident victims.
Timely emergency medical assistance to road accident victims.
The right to a speedy trial in criminal cases.
Providing equal employment opportunities in government hospitals.
questions.solution: The passage links the "Golden Hour" to Article 21 and the duty of hospitals to treat accident victims immediately.

questions.questionText:
Parliament passes a Constitutional Amendment that completely removes the power of Judicial
Review. The Supreme Court is asked to decide the validity of this amendment. According to the
ruling in Kesavananda Bharati mentioned in the passage, what is the likely outcome?
options: The amendment is valid because Parliament has absolute power to amend
The amendment is invalid because separation of powers is Basic Structure
The amendment is valid because the doctrine is not expressly mentioned
The amendment is invalid because only the President removes judicial powers
questions.solution: , as the passage notes that separation of powers is part of the Basic Structure and a feature that cannot be amended per the cited case.

questions.questionText: With reference to judicial review under the anti-defection law, which of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The Speaker's decision is completely immune from judicial review as it is a matter of internal legislative procedure.
The Speaker's decision can be challenged before courts only after it is made, and only on limited grounds such as mala fides or constitutional violations.
Courts can intervene at any stage of the proceedings before the Speaker to prevent possible injustice.
The President of India has the final authority to review the Speaker's decision in defection matters.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The Speaker's decision can be challenged before courts only after it is made, and only on limited grounds such as mala fides or constitutional violations. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
The "Right to a wholesome environment" was first read into Article 21 (Right to Life)
       by the Supreme Court in:
options: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Charan Lal Sahu v. Union of India
Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar
Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India

questions.questionText:
The Prime Minister is charged with corruption by CBI. He claims that as head of the executive
government, he enjoys executive immunity from prosecution and refuses to appear before the
ordinary courts. Based on Dicey's first pillar, can his claim succeed?
options: No, only if the charges are politically motivated by the opposition party
Yes, because executive authorities have special inherent prerogative powers in governance

Yes, because the Prime Minister holds the highest executive constitutional office in the
Union
No, because supremacy of law means no man is above the ordinary law of the land
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: No, because supremacy of law means no man is above the ordinary law of the land. Accordingly, option D is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, replaced several
       older laws to create a uniform system. Which of the following pairs of laws was
       specifically mentioned as being replaced by the 2015 Act?
options: The Indian Penal Code, 1860 and the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.

The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 and the Child
       Labour Act, 1986.

The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 and the Guardians and Wards Act,
       1890.
The Juvenile Justice Act, 2000 and the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.

questions.questionText:
A consumer court passed an interim order directing a company to deposit Rs. 1 lakh pending final
hearing. The company complied. Later, the final judgment was passed dismissing the consumer's
claim. Now the consumer files a fresh suit in a civil court on the same facts. Can this suit be
entertained?
options: No, because the interim order strictly operates as res judicata
Yes, because consumer court judgments never bind the civil courts
Yes, because interim orders never attract the res judicata bar
No, because the final judgment prevents further legal re-litigation
questions.solution: , as the consumer court passed a final judgment on merits dismissing the claim, which became final and conclusive between the parties, barring fresh litigation on the same matter.

questions.questionText:
Ritika purchased a sewing machine on deferred instalments from Sagar Appliances. She used
it personally from her home to stitch clothes for local customers and claimed that the income
was her only source of livelihood. Her younger brother occasionally helped her in cutting cloth
and packing finished garments. In a separate transaction, Nitin purchased twenty similar
machines from the same dealer under advance orders received from boutiques and also hired
repair services for maintaining those machines in his workshop. When defects appeared in the
machines, both Ritika and Nitin filed consumer complaints.
Consider the following statements:
I. Ritika is not a consumer because the consideration was under a system of deferred
payment and had not been fully paid at the time of complaint.
II. Ritika may remain a consumer if the sewing machine was bought and used exclusively for
earning livelihood by means of self-employment.
III. Nitin is excluded from the definition of consumer if the machines were obtained for resale
or for a profit-driven business purpose.
IV. Nitin may still be treated as a consumer for repair services because the commercial-
purpose exclusion applies only to goods and not to services.
How many of the above statements are incorrect?
options: One
Two
Three
Four	:	,
questions.solution: Statement I is incorrect because consideration may be under a system of deferred payment. Statement II is correct because livelihood through self-employment is protected from the commercial- purpose exclusion.

questions.questionText:
According to the passage, which of the following correctly lists the directions issued by the
Supreme Court regarding menstrual hygiene in schools?
options:
Free sanitary napkins, gender-segregated toilets, MHM corners with spare uniforms,
covered waste bins, and water supply were mandated for all schools.

Free sanitary napkins, menstrual leave for female students, private counselling rooms,
and nutritional supplements were directed by the Court for all schools.

Only government schools were required to install vending machines, while private schools
were directed only to maintain functional toilets and water supply.

The Court directed schools to provide biodegradable pads, health insurance for students,
incinerators in each classroom, and paid leave for female teachers.
questions.solution: The passage lists the following directions: functional gender-segregated toilets, continuous water supply, free oxo-biodegradable sanitary napkins through vending machines or distribution points, MHM corners with spare uniforms and hygiene materials, and covered waste bins. Option A captures all these accurately.

questions.questionText:
A driver momentarily miscalculates the distance of an oncoming car, resulting in a minor
collision with no injuries. Under the passage, does this act constitute criminal negligence?
options:
No, because it represents a mere error of judgment and lacks a high degree of disregard for
safety.

Yes, because any breach of a duty to take reasonable care instantly qualifies as criminal
negligence.

Yes, because the occurrence of a collision automatically proves the driver acted with gross
rashness.

Yes, because operating a vehicle always imposes the highest standard of care possible
under the law.
questions.solution: This is correct because a momentary miscalculation is merely an error of judgment, safely falling short of the gross rashness required for a criminal offense.

questions.questionText:
Considering the passage as a whole, which of the following most accurately states the ratio
(the operative legal basis) of the decision, as distinct from incidental observations?
options:
A religious congregation dissolved by its ecclesiastical authority automatically loses its
entire legal status and organizational standing.

A writ of habeas corpus cannot be issued if an adult's detention is proven voluntary, as
parental disagreement does not justify intervention.

Adult women who have attained the age of twenty-one enjoy a higher degree of
constitutional liberty than those below that specific age.

Statements recorded by police officers during an inquiry serve as absolute and conclusive
proof across all constitutional writ proceedings.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: A writ of habeas corpus cannot be issued if an adult's detention is proven voluntary, as parental disagreement does not justify intervention. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
According to the passage, what is the primary difference between the judicial review of
administrative decisions and the judicial review of legislative actions?
options: Legislative actions are immune to judicial review, while administrative actions are not.
Review of legislative action has wider parameters than administrative review.

Review of legislative action operates within narrower parameters compared to administrative
decisions.

Only the Supreme Court can review legislative actions, while only High Courts review
administrative ones.
questions.solution: The passage explicitly states that the "judicial review of legislative action operates within narrower parameters when compared to the review of administrative decisions." Incorrect Options:

questions.questionText:
To reduce traffic, a city enacts a law requiring all citizens, without any exceptions, to drive
their vehicles in reverse gear on Tuesdays. Does this law violate Article 14?
options: No, because the law has a specific objective of reducing traffic congestion.
Yes, because applying a completely irrational rule constitutes manifest arbitrariness.
No, because it applies equally to everyone and entirely avoids class legislation.
Yes, because it fails to classify citizens based on a distinguishing factor.
questions.solution: the passage explicitly states that a completely irrational or whimsical rule violates equality through "manifest arbitrariness," even if applied equally.

questions.questionText:
In the context of Article 356 of the Constitution of India, which of the following considerations is
most crucial for determining whether President’s Rule can be validly imposed in a State?
options: The ruling party’s election manifesto advocating a religious objective.
Isolated incidents of disturbance resulting in loss of life and property.
Breakdown of constitutional machinery.
The continuation in office of a Ministry after communal tension.
questions.solution: Article 356 can be invoked only when there is a breakdown of constitutional governance in a State. Mere disturbances, political ideology, or controversial manifesto promises are insufficient unless they result in an actual inability of the State Government to function in accordance with constitutional provisions, including adherence to secularism as part of the basic structure.

questions.questionText: F purchases a product solely based on an influencer's endorsement. Later, F discovers that the influencer had no experience using the product and merely repeated brand-provided scripts. Which of the following is the most legally appropriate conclusion?
options: The contract is automatically void due to misrepresentation.
The influencer cannot be held liable as they relied on the brand.
The consumer has no remedy since endorsements are opinions.
The consumer's consent may be vitiated due to misleading representation influencing the decision.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The consumer's consent may be vitiated due to misleading representation influencing the decision. Accordingly, option D is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Raju is in active police custody for theft. He tells the investigating officer, "I stole the gold
watch and buried it under the banyan tree." The police subsequently find the watch under the
tree. Based on the passage, which part of Raju's statement is admissible in court?
options: The complete statement because a physical fact was discovered.
No portion of the statement since he was in police custody.
Only the portion stating "I buried it under the banyan tree."
Only the portion stating "I stole the gold watch" as a confession.
questions.solution: it applies the rule of severability mentioned in the passage, admitting only the information that directly caused the discovery of the hidden stolen property.

questions.questionText: A group publishes content advocating secession of a region from India, but without calling for violence. The State restricts the content citing sovereignty and integrity of India. Which is the most appropriate conclusion?
options: The restriction is invalid as there is no incitement to violence.
The restriction is valid only if the content leads to public disorder.
The restriction is invalid as expression of political ideas is always protected.
The restriction may be valid as it concerns the sovereignty and integrity of India, even in absence of immediate violence.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The restriction may be valid as it concerns the sovereignty and integrity of India, even in absence of immediate violence. Accordingly, option D is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText: X agrees to employ Y on the condition that Y will forfeit all retirement benefits if Y marries during employment. Y marries and challenges the clause. Which is the best interpretation?
options: The clause is valid as it regulates service conditions and not marriage directly.
The clause is void because it imposes a financial penalty that effectively restrains marriage.
The clause is valid if Y had voluntarily accepted the employment terms.
The clause is enforceable as long as it applies only during employment.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The clause is void because it imposes a financial penalty that effectively restrains marriage. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
According to the passage, the Witness Protection Scheme, 2018 requires each State to
establish a Witness Protection Fund. Which of the following correctly identifies the sources
through which this Fund is to be constituted?
options:
Through Central Government grants, judicial fines collected from convicted accused, and
voluntary contributions from bar associations across States.

Through a combination of State budgetary allocations, United Nations Convention funds,
and penalty amounts recovered from persons who threaten witnesses.

Through State budgetary allocation, court-ordered costs/deposits, permitted
donations/contributions, and CSR funds.

Only through budgetary allocations made annually by the State Legislature and approved
by the Finance Ministry of the Central Government.
questions.solution: The passage explicitly states that each State is required to establish a Witness Protection Fund through State budgetary allocation, court-ordered costs/deposits, permitted donations/contributions, and CSR funds. Option C reproduces this accurately.

questions.questionText: Which of the following options best describes the difference between robbery and extortion under the Indian Penal Code?
options: In extortion, property is taken without consent, whereas in robbery, it is taken with consent.
In robbery, there is fear of instant harm and immediate delivery of property, whereas in extortion, such immediacy may be absent.
Extortion always involves violence, whereas robbery may not involve violence.
Robbery requires entrustment of property, whereas extortion does not.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: In robbery, there is fear of instant harm and immediate delivery of property, whereas in extortion, such immediacy may be absent. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText: Which of the following options, best describe an unpaid seller?
options: E, a seller received half payment in cash and half in kind.
F, a seller, received bill of exchange, which was honoured within the stipulated period.
G, a seller received half payment as cash and for other half a promise to pay was made.
H, a seller received a promissory note against the goods sold, which was later paid.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: G, a seller received half payment as cash and for other half a promise to pay was made. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
A state passes legislation allowing indefinite detention of individuals suspected of planning crimes,
without trial or periodic review. The detainees are provided food, shelter, and are not physically
harmed. Is this consistent with Article 21 as interpreted today?
options: Yes because the detainees’ physical needs are met and satisfied
No only if the detention exceeds one year under the new law

No because personal liberty includes freedom beyond physical well being

questions.questionText:
ABC Logistics hired Rajesh as a driver. While delivering a package during his work hours, Rajesh
drove over the speed limit and hit a pedestrian, causing injuries. The pedestrian sues ABC

options: No, because speeding is a personal choice of the employee

No, because the employer was not at fault for speeding

questions.solution: , as all three elements—a tort (accident), an employee relationship (Rajesh), and course of employment (delivering package)—are present.

questions.questionText: A novel contains explicit passages but is widely regarded as a critique of social oppression. The State bans it citing obscenity. Which is the most appropriate conclusion?
options: The ban is valid as any explicit material violates decency or morality.
The ban is valid only if the author intended to offend public morality.
The ban is likely invalid if the work, taken as a whole, possesses significant literary and social value despite explicit content.
The ban is valid as long as some sections of society find the material offensive.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The ban is likely invalid if the work, taken as a whole, possesses significant literary and social value despite explicit content. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
At a busy shopping mall, Meera notices a stranger's wallet falling from their pocket. She quickly picks

annoyed. Can the stranger successfully claim battery?
options: Yes, because Meera intentionally touched without prior permission from the stranger
Yes, because any unconsented touching in a non-emergency is always battery

No, because the touching was not offensive to a reasonable person's dignity

questions.questionText:

options: The organisation criticised the Government.
The organisation intended to influence public opinion.

Immediately upon the notification of the DPDP Rules in 2025, with no grace period

questions.questionText:
Which of the following best describes the Constitutional Mechanism provided by Article 13(2) as

options:
It acts as a prohibition that renders any law void if it takes away or abridges fundamental
rights.
It expands the power of judiciary to override legislative actions.
It provides a procedure for the legislature to amend the Constitution.
Both (a) and (b)
questions.solution: Article 13(2) is described as prohibiting the State from enacting laws that abridge fundamental rights and rendering such laws void to the extent of inconsistency. Incorrect Options:

questions.questionText: K agreed to organise a large public event for L on a specified date. Before the event, the government prohibited all public gatherings because of a nationwide emergency. Neither party contributed to the circumstances. Which option best applies?
options: The contract is frustrated because a legal prohibition has rendered performance impossible.
K has committed actual breach by failing to organise the event.
K has committed anticipatory breach because performance will not occur.
The contract remains enforceable because impossibility requires physical destruction.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The contract is frustrated because a legal prohibition has rendered performance impossible. Accordingly, option A is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Kavita entered into two arrangements on the same day. First, she orally promised to give %8
lakh to her nephew Nikhil “out of affection” after he completed his studies, but the promise
was neither written nor registered. Second, she agreed in writing to pay Rohan one
consolidated amount of 790,000 per month for managing her licensed food truck and also
arranging supplies for an unlicensed liquor counter operated from the same premises. When
disputes arose, both Nikhil and Rohan claimed enforcement of their respective promises.
Consider the following statements:
I. Nikhil’s claim is enforceable merely because the promise was made on account of natural
love and affection between near relatives
II. Rohan’s agreement is void if one consolidated consideration was fixed for both the lawful
food truck and the unlawful liquor counter.
III. A mere promise without something being given or promised in return is generally not
enforceable.
IV. If an agreement without consideration is made in writing and registered on account of
natural love and affection between near relations, it may be valid.
How many of the above statements are correct?
options: One
Two
Three
Four
questions.solution: Statement I is incorrect because Kavita’s promise to Nikhil was oral and unregistered, even though it was based on affection. Statement II is correct because Rohan’s agreement involves one consolidated consideration for lawful and unlawful purposes.

questions.questionText:
Indian cricketer Rishabh Pant is arrested by local police on vague charges of "creating a public
nuisance" during a peaceful charity event. No formal First Information Report (FIR) is filed, and his
family is denied access to him. His lawyer alleges illegal detention. Which writ is most appropriate to
secure his immediate release?
options: Mandamus, to command the police to file an FIR.
Certiorari, to quash the illegal arrest order issued.
Habeas Corpus, to produce him and test detention legality.
Quo Warranto, to question the police’s authority in the matter.
questions.solution: This is the classic use of Habeas Corpus when a person is allegedly detained unlawfully, to have the body brought before the court.

questions.questionText: A publication comments harshly on an ongoing judicial proceeding, suggesting bias and predicting outcomes. The court initiates action. Which is the best interpretation?
options: The publication is protected as criticism of institutions is part of free speech.
The publication is valid unless it directly interferes with the final judgment.
The publication may be restricted under contempt of court if it tends to prejudice or undermine judicial authority.
The publication is valid as long as it reflects personal opinion.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The publication may be restricted under contempt of court if it tends to prejudice or undermine judicial authority. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Vikram has wrongful possession of a vacant plot of land. The true legal owner, Anil, forcibly enters the
land to retake possession. Vikram sues Anil for trespass. Based on the specific exception mentioned in
the passage, does Vikram have a valid claim?
options: Yes, because a wrongful possessor can sue any person.
Yes, because Anil entered without Vikram's prior permission.
Yes, because trespass is actionable without proving damage.
None of the above arguments support a suit here.

questions.questionText:
A government hospital refuses to provide emergency medical treatment to accident victims who cannot

succeed?
options: No because Article 21 doesn't include free healthcare for citizens
Yes because life includes emergency healthcare from the state hospital
Yes only if families prove the hospital had adequate funds today
No because financial constraints justify the policy of the hospital

questions.questionText:
According to the passage, what was the only statutory exception to Section 28 of the Indian Contract
Act before the Mediation Act, 2023?
options: Agreements referring disputes to conciliation proceedings
Agreements referring disputes to arbitration
Agreements requiring parties to attempt negotiation before litigation
Agreements submitted to judicial officers for enforcement
questions.solution: Why B is correct: The passage explicitly states: "Prior to 2023, the only statutory exception to Section 28 was for arbitration agreements." It further elaborates: "This amendment places mediation on equal statutory footing with arbitration, which has enjoyed such protection since the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996." This clearly establishes that before the Mediation Act, only arbitration agreements were statutorily excepted from Section 28's prohibition on agreements restricting access

questions.questionText:
Consider these government actions:
I. Minister ignores court order citing executive privilege
II. Law giving President sole discretion to appoint judges
IIL. Police detain citizen without warrant or reason
Which action(s) MOST CLEARLY violate Dicey's Rule of Law pillars?
options: I and II only violate the constitutional scheme and Dicey’s formulation
II and III only violate the no-discretion and equality principles together
All three actions violate different but core aspects of Dicey’s Rule of Law
I only violates the idea that no one is above the authoritative law
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: All three actions violate different but core aspects of Dicey’s Rule of Law. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
What is the most fundamental reason why the law prohibits a direct transfer of

options:
Because an unborn person, not being a legal entity, lacks the capacity to accept

Because it is practically impossible to ascertain the identity and existence of an

Because such a transfer would create a significant risk of fraud and disputes

Because the law presumes that a transferor's primary intention is always to

questions.questionText: An independent journalist publishes investigative reports exposing corruption. While the government takes no action against him, several private organisations pressure advertisers to terminate contracts, publicly reveal his personal information, and threaten institutions hosting his lectures. Which option most appropriately follows?
options: No constitutional issue exists because only State action affects freedom of speech.
Constitutional concerns arise because private coercive conduct may substantially undermine free expression.
The conduct remains permissible because economic pressure forms part of ordinary public debate.
Constitutional concerns arise only if criminal proceedings are initiated.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: Constitutional concerns arise because private coercive conduct may substantially undermine free expression. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText: Based on the petitioners’ contentions in the passage, which of the following inferences is correct?
options: Any communal disturbance automatically amounts to a failure of constitutional machinery.

A State Government loses its secular character merely because its ruling party’s manifesto
contains religious objectives.

The presence of communal tension necessarily warrants the imposition of President’s Rule
under Article 356.

Limited incidents of violence do not, itself, justify that a State Government cannot be run as
per the Constitution.
questions.solution: Limited incidents of violence do not, by themselves, justify the conclusion that a State Government cannot be run in accordance with the Constitution. Incorrect Options:

questions.questionText:
A landscape artist was hired to plant 100 trees for a city project. Due to a technical flaw in the
tender process, the contract was declared void after 40 trees were planted. The city removed those
40 trees immediately and refused to use the artist's work. Can the artist claim quantum meruit?
options: Yes, because the contract was void due to a technical deficiency
No, because the measure of damages must be the full contract price
No, because the city did not receive any benefit from the work
Yes, because 40 trees were already planted and labor was performed
questions.solution: ; since the city removed the trees and did not use the work, they were not “unjustly enriched," which is the core concept of the remedy.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements most accurately captures the concept of
       ‘substantive equality’ as it is applied in the passage?
options:
All individuals, regardless of ability, must be treated in an identical manner and be
  subjected to the exact same digital verification processes.

The state must ensure that its laws and policies have the same outcome for all
  citizens, and any disparate impact on a particular group is unconstitutional.

Recognising that different groups face different barriers, the state must take active

The state must provide financial compensation to members of marginalised

questions.questionText:
The city civil court of Nagpur district starts hearing a matter which is out of its pecuniary jurisdiction. The city
civil court has jurisdiction in such matters to the amount of rupees 1,00,000. All matters of value above rupees
1,00,000 have to be heard by the High Court. The High Court of Bombay (Nagpur Bench) directs the court to
transfer the case to the High Court and not hear it any further. Decide which writ has been invoked here.
options: Certiorari
Prohibition
Quo Warranto
Habeas Corpus
questions.solution: The passage explains that the writ of Prohibition is issued by a superior court to prevent an inferior court or tribunal from proceeding with a matter over which it lacks jurisdiction. Since the City Civil Court was hearing a case beyond its pecuniary jurisdiction, @CLAT_OWNER the High Court rightly directed it not to proceed further. This is a classic instance of the writ of Prohibition. Therefore, Option B is correct. Why other options are incorrect: A. This is incorrect because Certiorari is generally used to quash or review a decision already

questions.questionText:
Based on the passage, what is the fundamental policy rationale underlying the CCTS's regulatory
surplus doctrine that creates tension with Rule 8 of the SWM Rules?
options:
Carbon credits should only be awarded for activities that generate measurable emissions
reductions of at least one ton of CO2 equivalent, excluding smaller-scale waste management

Carbon credits should reward genuine additional environmental action beyond what would
occur through legal compliance or business-as-usual scenarios, ensuring credits create real

Carbon credit markets must prioritize industrial energy efficiency projects over waste
management activities because waste sector emissions are already regulated under separate
environmental frameworks

Carbon credits cannot be issued for activities that simultaneously qualify for other incentive
mechanisms like Renewable Energy Certificates to prevent double counting across all
environmental credit systems
questions.solution: The passage states: "Carbon credits should reward additional environmental action, not mere compliance with legal obligations. Issuing credits for mandated activities would create windfall profits without genuine climate benefit" and further explains that "the CCTS regulatory surplus principle ensures carbon credits reward actions that would not have occurred under business-as-usual or legal compliance scenarios." This captures the core rationale for excluding mandated activities.

questions.questionText:
A contract is entered into for the sale of prohibited narcotic substances. One party
       later sues for breach. Based on the passage, what is the most appropriate legal
       outcome?
options: The contract is voidable at the option of the innocent party.
The contract is void and unenforceable from the beginning.
The contract is enforceable because consideration was paid.

questions.questionText:
According to the passage, what total amount of compensation did the Special Court order the
