questions.questionText:
Ramesh dies intestate, survived by his widow, a mother, and a paternal uncle. He has
       no children, and his father predeceased him. Who will inherit his property?
options:
The property will be divided equally between his widow and his mother as the
               closest relatives.

His widow, mother, and paternal uncle will all share the property equally as
               they are all legal heirs.

Only his widow and mother will inherit as Class I heirs, to the complete
               exclusion of the paternal uncle.

His paternal uncle will inherit as the sole surviving male agnate and the
               nearest blood relative.

questions.questionText:
A news website publishes a false report stating that Amitabh Bachchan has been critically ill and has
withdrawn from all public life. The report causes significant distress to Mr. Bachchan and his family.
However, it inadvertently leads to a massive outpouring of public sympathy and a surge in viewership
for his old films and TV shows, resulting in increased royalty payments for him. Can Mr. Bachchan sue
for defamation?
options: Yes, because publishing false facts injuring reputation is actionable.
No, because he suffered no real harm and in fact gained financially from it.
Yes, but he can only sue for the amount of the increased royalties he received.
No, because the news was related to health, which is a private matter.
questions.solution: Defamation protects the right to reputation. Its infringement (injuria) is actionable per se, regardless of resulting financial loss or gain.

questions.questionText:
Which line of reasoning would weaken the claim that the Preamble contains an inviolable Basic
Structure?
options: Difficulties in identifying which elements are part of the Basic Structure.
Demonstrating that the Preamble was voted upon by the Constituent Assembly.
Showing that the Preamble’s text was amended in 1976.
Citing constitutional provisions that allow amending powers.
questions.solution: If the Basic Structure is not clearly defined or if amending power is broad, the claim of an inviolable core is weakened. Incorrect Options:

questions.questionText:
The Court warned that State interference in such matters "would have a chilling effect on the
exercise of constitutional freedoms." Which scenario, drawn strictly from the logic of the
passage, best illustrates this "chilling effect"?
options:
Religious congregations voluntarily self-censoring their activities for fear of facing
mandatory state re-registration after local dissolution.

Police authorities hesitating to perform necessary legal inquiries into legitimate
allegations of unlawful or coerced detentions.

Parents feeling completely discouraged from approaching constitutional courts for any
form of legal grievance or judicial remedy.

Adults refraining from making independent choices about faith out of fear that relatives
might trigger state-backed judicial inquiries.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: Adults refraining from making independent choices about faith out of fear that relatives might trigger state-backed judicial inquiries. Accordingly, option D is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Alia Bhatt and Ranveer Singh, while watching an international chess championship, decide to bet =10
lakh on the outcome of a match between two grandmasters whom they do not personally know. Alia
predicts that Player A will win, while Ranveer backs Player B. They agree that whoever predicts
incorrectly will pay the other %10 lakh. Neither has any commercial, personal, or professional interest
in the chess match apart from the agreed stake.
options: No, it is a void wagering contract.
Yes, it is a valid contingent contract.
No, because the event is a game of skill.
Yes, as both parties freely consented.
questions.solution: They have no interest in the chess match beyond the stake. This is a classic wager on an uncertain event and is void.

questions.questionText:
Anjali went to a specialized paint store and told the owner she needed "weather-proof paint
specifically for an outdoor wooden deck." The owner recommended a particular brand. After one
rainstorm, the paint peeled off because it was actually meant for indoor walls. Is the seller liable?
options: No, because caveat emptor is the default rule for all private sales
Yes, but only if Anjali can prove the seller acted with fraudulent intent
Yes, because Anjali informed the seller of purpose and relied on expertise
No, because Anjali should have read the label on the paint can herself
questions.solution: , as the passage explicitly exempts cases where a specific purpose is communicated and the buyer relies on the seller's skill.

questions.questionText: J promises to pay K Rs. 5,00,000 if K's cargo safely reaches Mumbai port. Before the cargo reaches, the ship is hijacked and the cargo is irretrievably lost. What is the correct legal position?
options: The contract becomes void since the contingent event (safe arrival) has become impossible.
The contract becomes enforceable since loss has occurred.
The contract is a wager since outcome depended on chance.
The contract becomes enforceable after reasonable time.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The contract becomes void since the contingent event (safe arrival) has become impossible. Accordingly, option A is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
A start-up with eight women employees operates from a co-working space. An employee alleges that
during an official work meeting with a client at a café, the client made inappropriate remarks and
engaged in unwelcome physical contact. The employer is unsure how to proceed since the organization
has fewer than ten employees.
options: The employer must form an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) immediately.
The ICC cannot handle this as the incident occurred outside the office.
The employer should dismiss the complaint due to the small staff size.
The Local Complaints Committee (LCC) is the appropriate forum here.
questions.solution: The LCC is the appropriate forum for workplaces with fewer than ten employees.

questions.questionText:
An individual gives a private verbal speech in a closed-room family gathering that contains biased
remarks against a specific caste. No electronic recording is made, and the speech is not shared
with the public. Does this act fall under the scope of the Bill as described?
options: Yes, because it involves discrimination rooted in caste.
No, because the Bill covers communication made in public.
Yes, because any provocative speech is followed by violent incidents.
No, because the Bill only applies to electronic media and print, not verbal communication.
questions.solution: The legislation covers communication made "in public" through various means (verbal, print, etc.). Private conversations that are not disseminated or made in a public forum do not meet the criteria mentioned in the text.

questions.questionText:
An illegal gambling den in an apartment creates constant noise and disrupts
       neighborhood peace. A frustrated neighbor sues, asking a court to order it shut down.
       What is the likely result for the neighbor's request?
options:
The court will grant the injunction because the operation is a clear public
             nuisance.

The court cannot issue an injunction as such orders are only for private
             nuisance claims.

The neighbor cannot get an injunction; only the state can seek that remedy for
             a public nuisance.

The neighbor can get an injunction if they first prove a special injury from the
             noise.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements would the Supreme Court most likely disagree
       with, based on the passage?
options: Free speech protects unpopular and critical viewpoints.
Reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2) must be narrowly applied.

Speech that embarrasses the government can routinely be restricted to maintain
       stability.
The State bears responsibility to respect and preserve free expression.

questions.questionText:
The passage notes that BNSS introduces electronic records, gender-sensitive search
procedures, digital notices, and audio-video recording of search and seizure. What is the most
accurate inference about the primary objective of BNSS over CrPC?
options:
BNSS primarily aims to increase the punishments for proclaimed offenders by introducing
faster attachment proceedings.

BNSS seeks to modernise criminal procedure by incorporating digital safeguards and
strengthening protections for vulnerable groups.

BNSS primarily aims to transfer judicial powers of property disposal from Magistrates to
police officers for faster resolution.

BNSS replaces CrPC entirely with new provisions that have no structural correspondence
to the sections under CrPC.
S-20, Nandkishore Parikh Marg, Bapu Nagar, JAIPUR Ph. 7240060099 | www.lptedtech.com	34

LPT	Law Prep Mock Test Series
questions.solution: The passage consistently highlights BNSS features such as electronic records, gender-sensitive procedures, digital notice issuance, and audio-video recording of search and seizure — all pointing toward modernisation and enhanced protection. Option D is directly contradicted by the passage, which notes structural correspondence.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is not correct regarding Uniform civil code (UCC)
options:
A Uniform Civil Code (UCC) refers to a common law for personal matters such as marriage,
inheritance, divorce, adoption etc that applies to all religious communities.

Assam will be the second state after India's independence to implement the Uniform Civil
Code.
Uniform civil code is a subject of concurrent list.
None of the above
questions.solution: A Uniform Civil Code (UCC) refers to a common law for personal matters such as marriage, inheritance, divorce, adoption etc that applies to all religious communities. So option (a) is correct.

questions.questionText:
A seller told a buyer that a horse was "perfectly sound" knowing it suffered from recurring
lameness. The buyer purchased it relying on this statement and later sought rescission and
damages when the condition appeared.
options:
The statement is misrepresentation under Section 18; the buyer may rescind but cannot
claim damages as there was no fraudulent intent.

The buyer has no remedy as caveat emptor applies where the buyer had an opportunity to
inspect.

The statement is fraud as it was made with knowledge of its falsity to induce the contract;
the buyer may rescind and claim damages.
The statement is mere sales puffery with no legal consequences under the Contract Act.
questions.solution: A deliberate false statement of fact made to induce the contract satisfies Section 17. The buyer is entitled to rescind and sue for damages as fraud entitles both remedies.

questions.questionText:
Sara Ali Khan, a film producer, enters into a formal agreement with Ayushmann Khurrana to cast him
in her upcoming film project. The agreement states that Ayushmann will perform in the film only if it
receives its censor certificate from the appropriate authority by a specified deadline. Both parties
intend to proceed with the film’s production, subject to regulatory approval. The granting of the censor
certificate is uncertain at the time of agreement but is a standard prerequisite in the film industry.
options: A wagering contract on a government action.
A valid contingent contract.
An impossible contract from the start.
An agreement void for public policy.
questions.solution: The contract for acting services is contingent on a future uncertain event (censor approval), which is a common and valid business arrangement.

questions.questionText: A speaker delivers a speech calling for immediate violent protest against a law, urging listeners to "take action now." The State imposes restrictions citing incitement to an offence. Which is the best interpretation?
options: The restriction is valid as the speech has a direct and proximate connection to unlawful action.
The restriction is invalid as all political speech is absolutely protected.
The restriction is valid only if violence actually occurs following the speech.
The restriction is invalid unless the speaker intended to personally participate in the violence.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The restriction is valid as the speech has a direct and proximate connection to unlawful action. Accordingly, option A is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText: A railway operator failed to inspect tracks for several months despite internal reports warning of structural weakness. During routine weather conditions, the track fractured and caused derailment. The operator argues that the fracture was impossible to predict precisely and therefore inevitable.
options: The defence of inevitable accident is likely unavailable because ordinary precautions were neglected.
The defence succeeds because precise prediction of damage is unnecessary.
The defence succeeds because infrastructure failures are inherently unavoidable.
The defence succeeds because railway operators are not expected to conduct inspections.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The defence of inevitable accident is likely unavailable because ordinary precautions were neglected. Accordingly, option A is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
What is the fundamental point of contention between the Government and the Opposition
regarding the necessity of this Bill?
options:
The Government believes the police are currently too powerful, while the Opposition wants
more arrests.
Both parties agree that Article 19(1) should be suspended during communal unrest.

The Opposition wants the law to be non-cognizable, whereas the Government wants it to be
bailable.

The Government claims current laws lack "swift action," while the Opposition sees them as
adequate and fears political misuse.
questions.solution: Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok explicitly argued that existing provisions in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) were adequate and that the new law could be misused to target journalists.

questions.questionText:
A cafe owner bought an industrial blender, mentioning she needed it for crushing ice
       daily. The blender functions perfectly for general mixing but jams consistently with
       ice. She seeks to return it. What is the outcome?
options:
She is only entitled to damages covering the cost of a separate ice-crushing
             attachment for the blender.

She can return it only if she can prove the seller fraudulently guaranteed its
             ice-crushing capability.

She cannot return it because the blender is of satisfactory quality for standard
             blending tasks.

She may reject it as the goods are unfit for the particular purpose she made
             known to the seller.

questions.questionText: L, a police officer acting in good faith, attempts to arrest M. M resists the arrest and attacks L, causing serious injury, claiming he believed the arrest to be unlawful. Which of the following is most accurate?
options: M is protected since he believed the arrest was unlawful.
M is protected because private defence applies against all acts.
M is protected only if the arrest was actually unlawful.
M is not protected unless there was reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: M is not protected unless there was reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt. Accordingly, option D is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
The Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, which contains the anti-defection law, was inserted
by which constitutional amendment?
options: Forty-second Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
Forty-fourth Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978
Fifty-second Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985
Ninety-first Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003
questions.solution: The Tenth Schedule was inserted into the Constitution by the Fifty-second Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985. It introduced the anti-defection framework to curb political defections by elected members.

questions.questionText:
A male team leader frequently makes jokes containing sexual innuendos during weekly team meetings
attended by all staff. These remarks are often accompanied by suggestive laughter and create visible
discomfort among employees. A female team member feels humiliated and anxious before meetings,
and her concentration and performance have been affected. Though she has not confronted him
directly, she believes the environment has become hostile and intimidating.
options: This can constitute sexual harassment by creating a hostile work environment.
No harassment occurs as the jokes are not targeted at any specific individual.
She must first give a written complaint to her employer to establish the act.
Such conduct is only prohibited if it involves explicit physical contact.
questions.solution: The Act defines sexual harassment broadly to include verbal conduct like sexually colored remarks that create an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment, even if not directed at a specific person.

questions.questionText:
The principle of "Equal Protection of the Laws" under Article 14 is essentially an obligation for the
State to:
options: Ensure every citizen has an equal amount of wealth.
Treat equals equally and unequals unequally.
Abolish all forms of private property.
Provide identical punishments for every type of crime.
questions.solution: Equal protection means that the law should be applied similarly to people in similar circumstances (Equals among equals).

questions.questionText:
A state legislature passes a law mandating that all prisoners, regardless of their sentence duration, will
be kept in solitary confinement. Prisoners challenge this claiming it violates their dignity. Based on the
passage, which argument is strongest?
options: The law only affects convicted criminals so Article 21 doesn't apply
The law is procedurally valid as it was passed by legislature
Prisoners lose their Article 21 rights upon conviction by a court
The right to life includes dignity so solitary confinement is wrong

questions.questionText: G agrees to buy goods from H if a pending government notification lifting import restrictions is issued within 6 months. After 2 months, the government formally announces that no such notification will be issued. Which of the following is the most accurate legal outcome?
options: The contract becomes enforceable immediately since the uncertainty is resolved.
The contract remains valid until expiry of 6 months.
The contract becomes enforceable since parties intended to transact commercially.
The contract becomes void as the contingent event has become impossible before the stipulated time.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The contract becomes void as the contingent event has become impossible before the stipulated time. Accordingly, option D is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Which amendment is most closely associated with granting daughters equal coparcenary
rights under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956?
options: Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2001
Hindu Minority Amendment Act, 1999
Hindu Marriage Amendment Act, 1976
Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005
questions.solution: The Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005 amended Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act and gave daughters the status of coparceners in the same manner as sons. The amendment came into effect from 9 September 2005.

questions.questionText:
A city imposes a blanket ban on all public gatherings for two months citing “anticipated
     disturbances” based on an unverified intelligence note. Protestors challenge the order.
     Based on the passage, which outcome is most consistent with constitutional principles?
options:
The ban is valid because the State may restrict assemblies whenever public order
concerns arise.

The ban is unconstitutional because restrictions must be proximate, evidence-based,
and proportionate.

The ban is valid because assemblies are always subject to administrative
convenience.
The ban is constitutional only if protestors belong to political groups.

questions.questionText:
In his judgment, Justice Viswanathan expressed a specific concern about the consequences of
        invalidating Section 17A entirely. What was this major concern?
options:
It would automatically disqualify all public servants accused of corruption from holding
        office until proven innocent.

It would transfer the burden of proof from the prosecution to the accused public servant in all
        corruption cases.

It would lead to a concentration of power in the hands of the Central Bureau of Investigation,
        creating an investigative monopoly.

It would allow for the immediate registration of FIRs and coercive investigations, even on
        frivolous or motivated complaints.

questions.questionText:
Deepika Padukone and Anushka Sharma, during a casual industry gathering, begin discussing box-
office predictions for upcoming film releases. Deepika confidently claims that her next film will cross
%200 crore at the box office. Anushka disagrees and challenges her prediction. They agree that if
Deepika’s film grosses more than %200 crore, Anushka will pay her %5 lakh; if it fails to do so, Deepika
will pay Anushka 25 lakh. Neither actress has invested in or holds any financial interest in the other’s
film; the arrangement is purely a speculative wager between them.
options: A valid contract based on mutual promise.
An illegal agreement forbidden by statute.
A void wagering agreement under the law.
A lawful contingent contract for services.
questions.solution: The agreement fits the definition: payment depends on an uncertain box-office outcome, and neither has a genuine interest in the event beyond the bet.

questions.questionText: A scholarship policy allocates educational resources solely based on existing performance rankings without considering whether historically disadvantaged groups face structural barriers affecting their opportunities. Which approach most closely follows the passage?
options: The policy should be examined primarily from the perspective of individuals already benefiting from existing structures.
The policy should be assessed only by examining average economic outcomes.
The policy should be evaluated from the standpoint of individuals whose voices or interests remain marginalised.
The policy should automatically be upheld because identical treatment always guarantees equality.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The policy should be evaluated from the standpoint of individuals whose voices or interests remain marginalised. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText: The Supreme Court dismissed the petition under Article 32 primarily because:
options:
The petitioner had failed to demonstrate any violation of fundamental rights before the
Supreme Court and had not placed sufficient material on record to justify the invocation of the
apex court's extraordinary writ jurisdiction

The petition was filed despite a similar matter already being pending before the Bombay High
Court, making it a gross misuse of the court's process

The petitioner had approached the Supreme Court without first exhausting the statutory
remedies available under the relevant legislation governing the subject matter of the dispute

The bench found that the petition involved purely state-level administrative issues that fell
squarely within the territorial and subject-matter jurisdiction of the Bombay High Court alone
questions.solution: is correct because the passage explicitly states that the bench dismissed the petition on the ground that "the petitioner had approached the apex court directly despite a similar plea already being heard by the Bombay High Court," terming it a "gross misuse of the process of the court and of law."

questions.questionText:
The passage states that various High Courts adopted "divergent approaches" to mandatory mediation
clauses before 2023, with some voiding them and others taking a "pragmatic view, treating such clauses
as merely regulating the manner of enforcement." What does this judicial divergence primarily reveal
about the pre-2023 legal framework?
options: High Courts deliberately ignored statutory provisions to promote alternative dispute resolution
Arbitration agreements faced similar judicial uncertainty despite statutory protection

The Indian Contract Act was fundamentally incompatible with modern dispute resolution
practices

Section 28's language was ambiguous regarding whether procedural prerequisites constituted
absolute restrictions
questions.solution: Why D is correct: The judicial divergence reveals genuine ambiguity in interpreting Section 28's prohibition on agreements "absolutely restricting" access to courts. Some courts interpreted mandatory mediation as an "absolute restriction" (preventing immediate court access), while others saw it pragmatically as merely "regulating the manner of enforcement" (requiring a procedural step before court access).

questions.questionText:
Under the DPDPA, what is a core compliance requirement for organisations classified
         as "data fiduciaries" regarding security incidents?
options:
They must conduct a yearly internal audit and submit a detailed incident report to the
Data Protection Board.

They are required to report any significant data breach to the affected users within a 7-
day period from its discovery.

They must report data breaches to the relevant authorities within a strict timeframe of
72 hours.

They are obligated to formally notify the Ministry of Electronics and Information
Technology within 30 days of the incident.

questions.questionText:
A new law exempts industrial projects below 10 hectares from mandatory climate impact
assessment, citing ease of doing business. Several small plants collectively lead to severe local
air pollution and erratic rainfall patterns, increasing asthma cases among slum dwellers.
Which inference correctly applies the Court's ruling in MK. Ranjitsinh?
options:
The exemption can stand as long as each project individually meets minimum legal
standards under existing environmental laws

The cumulative climate harm violates the right to life and equality by neglecting
foreseeable environmental impacts on vulnerable populations

Economic growth takes precedence over fundamental rights under Article 21 when projects
promote ease of doing business

Judicial review cannot extend to legislative policy choices involving economic
considerations and industrial development strategies
questions.solution: The passage states that M.K. Ranjitsinh recognized protection from climate change as a fundamental right under Articles 21 and 14, "emphasizing the disproportionate impact on vulnerable populations including the poor." The scenario describes cumulative harm (air pollution, health impacts on slum dwellers) from collectively exempt projects, directly implicating climate rights and equality concerns central to the judgment.

questions.questionText:
A 20-year-old Hindu man marries a 17-year-old Hindu woman in a traditional
         ceremony. They are second cousins. The bride's parents challenge the marriage. Based
         solely on the Hindu Marriage Act, what is its status?
options:
The marriage is perfectly valid as their community custom permits the relationship
between the parties.

The marriage is voidable at the option of the bride's parents because the bride was
underage at the time of the solemnization.
The marriage is void due to the parties being sapindas.

The marriage would be valid if they immediately registered it, as registration can cure
such minor statutory non-compliances.

questions.questionText:
Karan used his personal savings from a salaried job to purchase a house. He lives
       there with his wife and children. Upon his death, how will this house be classified for
       the purpose of succession under the Hindu Succession Act?
options: It is coparcenary property as it was used for the benefit of his joint family.
It is separate or self-acquired property, distinct from any ancestral property.

It becomes ancestral property as it was acquired during his lifetime for the use of his
       family.

It is not subject to succession laws since it was purchased with his own salary and
       effort.

questions.questionText:
An art gallery, Galleria Moderna, offers to host an exclusive exhibition for an emerging artist, Arnav, with a
deadline for acceptance set for May 5th. The gallery also mentions that if Arnav does not respond by the deadline,
they may consider other artists. Arnav, intending to accept, drafts an acceptance email but, due to internet issues,
fails to send it before the deadline. Unaware of this, Galleria Moderna, on May 6th, extends the offer to another
artist, Riya, who accepts immediately. Arnav's email is finally sent and reaches the gallery on May 7th. Given the
circumstances and legal principles, which of the following statements are correct?
i. Galleria Moderna's contract with Arnav is valid because Arnav intended to accept before the deadline.
ii. Galleria Moderna's contract with Riya is valid as Arnav's acceptance was communicated after the deadline.
iii. Arnav's delayed communication does not affect the validity of his contract due to technical issues.
iv. Galleria Moderna should have waited longer before offering the exhibition to another artist.
options: Statements ii and iii
Statement ii
Statements i and iv
Statement iv
questions.solution: The passage explains that an offer is revoked by lapse of time if acceptance is not communicated within the prescribed period. Galleria Moderna clearly fixed May 5th as the deadline for acceptance. Although Arnav intended to accept before the deadline, his acceptance was not communicated until May 7th. By then, the original offer had already lapsed, allowing the gallery to validly offer the exhibition to Riya, who accepted it. Therefore, only Statement ii is correct. @CLAT_OWNER Why other options are incorrect:

questions.questionText:
Sarah, an accountant at a firm, went to a supermarket during her lunch break to buy groceries for
her home. On her way back to the office, she accidentally tripped a shopper with her bag. The
shopper sues Sarah's firm. Will the firm be held vicariously liable?
options: No, because the act was not committed in course of employment
Yes, because the firm benefits from Sarah being well-fed at work
No, because tripping someone is not a typical risk of accounting
Yes, because Sarah is currently a full-time employee of the firm
questions.solution: , since a lunch break for personal grocery shopping is generally considered outside the course of employment.

questions.questionText:
The 23rd Law Commission opined that the proposed 'One Nation One Election' Bills do not
        require ratification by the states. What is the constitutional basis for this opinion as
        mentioned?
options:
The Bills do not amend any of the subjects listed under clauses (a) to (e) of Article 368(2)
        which mandate state ratification.
The subject of elections is in the Union List, where Parliament has exclusive power.

The Supreme Court in a prior judgment exempted election-related amendments from state
        ratification.

The Bills are being introduced under Article 123 (Ordinance power) which does not require
        state consent.

questions.questionText:
Ranveer Singh is known for his unique and vibrant fashion sense. A popular menswear brand, without
his permission, uses a digitally altered image of his face on their billboards, making it appear he
endorses their products. Ranveer suffers no financial loss from this, and the brand's sales do not affect
his own income. However, he feels his personal and professional image has been misappropriated. Can
Ranveer seek a legal remedy?
options: No, because public figures implicitly consent to such commercial use of their image.
Yes, because his right to control his likeness was violated, which is actionable per se.
No, as he must first prove that the brand's profits increased due to his image.
Yes, but only if he can show he suffered measurable financial harm.
questions.solution: The unauthorized use infringes his personality right, an injuria actionable without proof of loss, fitting Injuria Sine Damnum.

questions.questionText: P entered into a contract with Q to transport luxury furniture to another city for Rs. 10 lakh. Before performance began, fuel prices increased sharply and transportation costs nearly doubled. P refused to perform, arguing that the contract had become commercially burdensome and economically impractical. Which of the following is most appropriate?
options: The contract is frustrated because increased expense automatically creates impossibility.
P is discharged because commercial hardship and reduced profitability excuse performance.
P has committed breach because increased cost alone does not amount to frustration.
P is discharged because contracts become void whenever circumstances change significantly.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: P has committed breach because increased cost alone does not amount to frustration. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText: A is attacked by B with a knife in an isolated area. A manages to disarm B, who falls to the ground unconscious. Despite this, A continues to strike B multiple times, resulting in B's death. Which of the following is the most legally appropriate conclusion?
options: A is completely protected as the right of private defence permits causing death in response to a deadly attack.
A is protected as long as the initial aggression was unlawful.
A is not liable since the entire act forms part of the same transaction.
A may lose the protection of private defence as the force used exceeded what was necessary after the threat had ceased.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: A may lose the protection of private defence as the force used exceeded what was necessary after the threat had ceased. Accordingly, option D is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) was asked to resolve a maritime boundary dispute
between India and a neighbouring country. India’s legal team cited multiple ICJ precedents and
UNCLOS provisions to justify its claim, while the other country relied on customary maritime
practices. Which comparative principle is demonstrated here?
options: Legal transplants, adopting foreign law directly into domestic law.
Codification, converting customary international practices into domestic statutes
Judicial precedent, using international decisions as persuasive authority.
Diplomatic immunity, exempting states from enforcement obligations abroad.
questions.solution: Option (a): Incorrect. Legal transplants involve formal adoption, not mere citation. Option (b): Incorrect. Codification involves formally enacting laws or rules into domestic statutes. Option (c): Correct. International precedents serve as persuasive authority in disputes. Option (d): Incorrect. Immunity is unrelated to maritime adjudication. Reference: "courts refer to international precedents, foreign judgments, and global conventions to interpret laws and resolve disputes."

questions.questionText:
Under the CrPC, attachment of property under Section 83 applies to a specific category of
persons. Which of the following correctly identifies that category?
options:
Persons who are accused of offences committed outside India and whose property is linked
to foreign criminal activity.

Persons who have been declared proclaimed offenders under Section 82 of the CrPC by a
competent Magistrate.

Persons who are found in possession of stolen property and against whom a chargesheet
has been filed in court.

Persons who have failed to appear before court despite summons but have not yet been
declared proclaimed offenders.
questions.solution: The passage clearly states that Section 83 CrPC applies to 'proclaimed offenders declared under Section 82.' Option A describes Section 105 CrPC, which deals with property linked to offences outside India — a separate provision. Options C and D describe persons not covered by Section 83 as described in the passage.

questions.questionText: E and F agree that E will pay F Rs. 1,00,000 if it rains in Jaipur on 1st July, and F will pay E Rs.1,00,000 if it does not rain. Both parties are tourists with no agricultural or commercial interest. Which of the following best characterizes this agreement?
options: A contingent contract dependent on uncertain weather conditions.
A valid agreement since both parties have equal chances of gain and loss.
A wager agreement as neither party has any interest apart from the stake.
A contingent contract enforceable upon occurrence of rain.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: A wager agreement as neither party has any interest apart from the stake. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Japan and India signed an extradition treaty. A Japanese national accused of financial fraud fled
to India, and Japan formally requested his surrender. India must assess whether to extradite him
considering treaty terms, domestic law, and potential political offense exceptions. Which principle
guides India’s decision?
options: Reciprocity, considering if Japan would extradite Indian nationals.
Customary law, allowing India to refuse extradition for political offences.
Comity of nations, mandating automatic surrender regardless of domestic law.

Treaty-based obligations, enforcing extradition while respecting domestic and international
law.
questions.solution: Option (a): Incorrect. Reciprocity influences but is not the primary guiding principle. Option (b): Incorrect. Political offence exceptions apply only in specific circumstances. Option (c): Incorrect. Comity is discretionary, not a binding rule. Option (d): Correct. Treaties require adherence to obligations while respecting domestic law. Reference: "These treaties often include dispute resolution clauses, investor protections, or obligations to surrender fugitives."

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly distinguishes between the right of lien and the right of stoppage in transit under the Sale of Goods Act?
options: Right of lien can be exercised even after the seller has parted with possession, whereas stoppage in transit requires possession with the seller.
Right of lien is available only when the buyer becomes insolvent, whereas stoppage in transit is available in all cases of non-payment.
Right of lien is exercised while the seller retains possession of goods, whereas stoppage in transit is exercised after the seller has parted with possession but the goods are still in transit.
There is no substantial difference between the two rights as both arise only after delivery of goods to the buyer.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: Right of lien is exercised while the seller retains possession of goods, whereas stoppage in transit is exercised after the seller has parted with possession but the goods are still in transit. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Ayesha visits a Delhi electronics showroom and sees a shelf tag reading, “4K TV %29,999 Today
Only.” She immediately asks the cashier to bill the TV at that price. Before billing, the manager
says the tag was placed by mistake and refuses to sell at 729,999. Ayesha sues. Who is more likely
to succeed?
options:
Ayesha, because selecting the TV and offering payment converts the displayed tag into a
binding commitment by the store.

Ayesha, because retail customers can enforce any printed price representation shown on a
shop display without further assent.

The manager, because “shop displays are not offers but invitations to offer,” so the store must
still assent at billing.

The manager, because any displayed price becomes unenforceable once the store claims it was
a staff error before billing.
questions.solution: The reference line states that “shop displays... are not offers but invitations to offer,” meaning they invite negotiation and the customer's offer at the counter.

questions.questionText:
A contract between two companies states that Mumbai shall be the “seat” of arbitration, while
hearings may be conducted in Bengaluru for convenience. The arbitral tribunal conducts all
hearings in Bengaluru and pronounces the award there. One party challenges the award
before the Bengaluru courts. Applying the reasoning of JKERA v. Rash Builders, which of the
following is accurate?
options:
Bengaluru courts alone have jurisdiction because hearings and award delivery occurred
there.
Both Mumbai and Bengaluru courts have concurrent jurisdiction.
Mumbai courts alone possess jurisdiction because Mumbai is the designated seat.
Jurisdiction depends solely on where the arbitral award was signed.
questions.solution: Option A — Incorrect This option incorrectly equates the venue with the seat. The Supreme Court clarified that the venue is merely a place chosen for convenience and does not determine supervisory jurisdiction.

questions.questionText: A functioning hospital secretly stores military ammunition in one wing of its premises. Without warning, the opposing force immediately launches a full-scale attack on the entire hospital complex. Which option is most appropriate?
options: The attack is automatically lawful because hospitals permanently lose protection after any misuse.
The attack may still raise legal concerns because withdrawal of protection may require reasonable warning.
The attack is unlawful because hospitals can never lose protection under any circumstances.
The attack is lawful because medical facilities are treated as ordinary buildings during war.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The attack may still raise legal concerns because withdrawal of protection may require reasonable warning. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Ravi approaches Suresh in a park and shows him a pistol tucked in his belt, saying, "Hand
over your gold chain immediately, or I will shoot your son who is playing over there." Suresh,
terrified, removes his gold chain and gives it to Ravi on the spot. Ravi takes the chain and
leaves. Has Ravi committed robbery?
options:
No, because this situation amounts to extortion since Suresh consented to give the chain
under fear created by Ravi.

No, because robbery requires actual physical injury, and mere threat without harm does
not satisfy the requirement of robbery.

Yes, because Ravi was present, created fear of instant death and obtained delivery of
movable property immediately.

Yes, because showing a pistol automatically converts any transfer of property into robbery
irrespective of the surrounding facts.
SCAN the OR for TECS
questions.solution: This is correct. All elements are satisfied: presence of the offender, fear of instant death to another person, and immediate delivery of movable property.

questions.questionText:
Based on the passage, which of the following statements best captures the distinction between
the "seat" and "venue" of arbitration as clarified by the Supreme Court?
options:
The seat and the venue are interchangeable terms, and either may be used to determine
the supervisory jurisdiction of courts over arbitral proceedings.

The seat refers to the place where the arbitral award is pronounced, whereas the venue
refers to the place where the arbitration agreement is signed.

The seat is the juridical home of arbitration that determines supervisory jurisdiction, while
the venue is merely a geographically convenient place for conducting hearings.

The venue determines jurisdiction over the arbitration, while the seat is significant only
for procedural rules followed by the arbitrator.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The seat is the juridical home of arbitration that determines supervisory jurisdiction, while the venue is merely a geographically convenient place for conducting hearings. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Based on the passage, what is the most significant consequence of the historical
      omission of the draft clauses on "resolutory conditions" from the final Indian
      Contract Act, 1872?
options:
It has made it impossible for parties in India to include legally valid force
    majeure clauses in their contracts.

It has forced Indian courts to incorrectly apply Section 32, which deals with the
    formation of obligations, to situations involving the termination of existing
    obligations.

It has led to the Indian judiciary relying exclusively on English case law to
    interpret force majeure clauses, ignoring the Contract Act entirely.

It has simplified the Indian Contract Act by removing a complex and
    unnecessary legal concept, thereby promoting greater clarity.

questions.questionText:
An illegal dumpster blocks a public alley. A florist's rear delivery entrance is
       completely blocked, spoiling perishable stock. The florist sues and proves the public
       nuisance and their unique financial harm. What remedy can they get?
options:
They are entitled to both an injunction against the defendant and monetary
             damages.

They are entitled only to have city authorities remove the dumpster, not to any
             money.
They are entitled to a court order for the defendant to remove the dumpster.

They are entitled to financial compensation for their distinct losses, like the
             ruined stock.

questions.questionText:
According to the passage, what is the minimum and maximum term of imprisonment prescribed
under Section 27(d) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940?
options: Not less than six months and up to one year
Not less than one year and up to two years
Not less than two years and up to five years
Up to three years with no minimum term specified
questions.solution: The passage clearly states: "Since Section 27(d) provides for imprisonment of not less than one year and up to two years..." This directly answers the question. Option (A) incorrectly states six months to one year, which is not mentioned anywhere in the passage.

questions.questionText:
On which of the following specific grounds does Article 14 explicitly prohibit the State from
discriminating?
options: Religion, Race, Caste, Language, and Sex.
Religion, Race, Caste, Sex, and Place of Birth.
Religion, Caste, Sex, Descent, and Residence.
Race, Caste, Profession, Sex, and Religion.
questions.solution: The text of Article 14 specifically lists: Religion, Race, Caste, Sex, and Place of Birth.

questions.questionText:
Statement: A six-month psychological study conducted on corporate professionals found that those
who practiced bonsai cultivation as a hobby reported a 42% reduction in self-reported stress levels
and showed measurably lower cortisol concentrations in blood tests compared to a matched control
group.
Conclusions:
I. Bonsai cultivation should be prescribed as the primary medical treatment for all stress-related
disorders in corporate environments.
II. Engaging in mindful horticultural activities such as bonsai cultivation may have measurable
physiological and psychological stress-reducing effects.
III. The control group in the study was composed entirely of individuals who had never experienced
any form of occupational stress.
IV. There appears to be a meaningful association between patient, detail-oriented hobbies and
reduced biological stress markers in working professionals.
options: Only I and III follow
Only I follows
Only II and III follow
Only II and IV follow
questions.solution: Conclusion I: Bonsai cultivation should be prescribed as the primary medical treatment for all stress-related disorders in corporate environments. This does NOT follow.

questions.questionText:
The High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections (2023), headed by former
          President Ram Nath Kovind, recommended a mechanism to synchronise elections.
          It stated that the President will declare a specific date to serve as the reference
          point for aligning assembly terms. What is this date called in the
          recommendation?
options: The synchronisation date
The election date
The notification date
The appointed date

questions.questionText:
Which legal doctrine did the Supreme Court apply in its recall order to argue that the
       absolute prohibition of ex post facto ECs could lead to disproportionate harm to
       public interest, thus needing a balanced approach?
options: Doctrine of Absolute Liability
Doctrine of Public Trust
Principle of Proportionality
Principle of Non-Retrogression

questions.questionText:
Mohan sued Sohan for damages arising from a road accident. The suit was dismissed by the trial
court for lack of jurisdiction. Mohan then files a fresh suit in the appropriate competent court
seeking the same damages from the same accident. Will res judicata apply?
options: Yes, because the parties and the issues are entirely identical
No, because the first court lacked the required legal jurisdiction
Yes, because one dismissal bars all future suits for damages
No, because dismissals never attract the principle of res judicata
questions.solution: , as the passage explicitly requires competent jurisdiction as a necessary element; a court lacking jurisdiction cannot pass a judgment that operates as res judicata.

questions.questionText:
The passage highlights that Justice Viswanathan cited the authority of the Lokpal to support
        his view. What specific example did he use to illustrate the robustness of an independent
        sanctioning authority?
options:
The Lokpal's authority to conduct an inquiry into an allegation of corruption even against the
        Prime Minister.

The Lokpal's role in supervising all police investigations into economic offenses across the
        country.

The Lokpal's mandate to provide prior approval for the prosecution of judges of the Supreme
        Court.
The Lokpal's power to directly impose penalties on convicted public servants without a trial.

questions.questionText:
Amit is accused of theft punishable with up to three years imprisonment. He wishes to
       apply for plea bargaining. The victim is willing to negotiate. Is Amit eligible for plea
       bargaining?
options:
Yes, as the offence is not punishable with death, life imprisonment, or
              imprisonment exceeding seven years.

No, because theft is specifically excluded from plea bargaining as it affects the
              socio-economic condition of the country.

Yes, but only if the offence is also compoundable under Section 320 of the
              CrPC.

No, because the victim's willingness compromises the voluntary nature of the
              plea.

questions.questionText:
The Court in this judgment applied the doctrine of substantive equality rather than formal
equality. Which of the following most accurately explains the difference as reflected in the
passage?
options:
Formal equality requires that all individuals be treated identically, while substantive
equality requires the State to address real structural disadvantages that prevent equal
outcomes.

Formal equality focuses only on legislation, while substantive equality applies exclusively
to judicial directions issued by the Supreme Court in PIL matters.

Substantive equality holds that women must receive more rights than men, while formal
equality insists on identical rights regardless of biological differences between groups.

Formal equality protects civil and political rights, while substantive equality exclusively
concerns itself with economic and social rights under the Directive Principles.
questions.solution: The passage states that substantive equality 'requires the State to address real disadvantages rather than treating everyone identically,’ and that the State must take ‘affirmative measures’ so biological differences don't result in unequal opportunity. Option A precisely captures this distinction.

questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): Courts emphasise that EIA is a substantive safeguard, not a procedural
     formality.
Reason (R): A project proponent may bypass public consultation if the Expert Appraisal
Committee permits it.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.

questions.questionText:
Who among the following is not a consumer under Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection
Act, 2019?
options:
Meera bought a laptop on deferred payment for preparing online classes for students and
used it personally to earn her livelihood from home.

Arvind purchased a water purifier for his parents, who used it at home with his approval
after he paid part of the price.

Kavita purchased fifty mixer-grinders from a dealer to resell them through her kitchen-
appliance shop during the festive season.

Rohan hired an online accounting course for his sister, who used the classes with his
approval while the fee remained partly promised.
questions.solution: Kavita is not a consumer because she purchased fifty mixer-grinders for resale through her appliance shop. The passage expressly excludes a person who obtains goods for resale or for any commercial purpose from the definition of consumer.

questions.questionText: A State government prohibits all online discussion regarding a controversial urban redevelopment project after discovering that a few individuals had posted threatening messages concerning the project. The order bans every discussion, including academic debate and criticism. Which option best follows?
options: The order appears disproportionate because restrictions must not exceed what is necessary to achieve a legitimate objective.
The order is justified because some unlawful speech permits complete suppression of related discussions.
The order is justified because administrative convenience outweighs expressive interests.
The order is constitutional because public projects cannot be criticised during implementation.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The order appears disproportionate because restrictions must not exceed what is necessary to achieve a legitimate objective. Accordingly, option A is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Prakash and Ritesh were co-owners of a small ancestral house. Ritesh threatened Prakash
that unless Prakash signed documents giving up his share in the house, Ritesh would publicly
circulate damaging allegations about Prakash’s daughter. Fearing injury to his family’s
reputation, Prakash signed and handed over the relinquishment documents. In another
incident, Sameer quietly removed Prakash’s mobile phone from his bag without his consent
and left the place without making any threat.
Consider the following statements:
I. Ritesh’s act cannot amount to extortion because delivery under extortion is limited to
movable property.
II. Ritesh’s act may amount to extortion because compelling a person by fear to give up a
share in a house may fall within delivery.
III. Sameer’s act may fall closer to theft because movable property was taken without the
consent of the victim.
IV. Sameer’s act may amount to extortion because Prakash lost property, even though
Prakash did not deliver it due to fear of injury.
How many of the above statements are incorrect?
options: One
Two
Three
Four
questions.solution: Statement I is incorrect because delivery under extortion is not limited to movable property. Statement II is correct because compelling a person by fear to give up a share in a house may amount to extortion.

questions.questionText:
In a Joint Hindu Family governed by Mitakshara law, the common ancestor A is
       survived by his son B, granddaughter C (B's daughter), and great-grandson D (C's
       son). All were born after 2005. Who among them is a coparcener?
options:
Only A and B are coparceners, as the line of coparcenary traditionally ends with the
       son.

Only A, B, and D are coparceners, as D is a male lineal descendant within three
       generations.

A, B, C, and D are all coparceners, as the daughter is a coparcener by birth with equal
       rights.

Only A is a coparcener, as the coparcenary requires a living common ancestor to
       sustain it.

questions.questionText:
Rohan has been illegally occupying a vacant apartment owned by Mr. Gupta for the past six months.
One day, Mr. Gupta enters the apartment using his spare key to inspect the property. Rohan files a suit
for trespass against Mr. Gupta, claiming his possession was disturbed. Will Rohan succeed in his suit
against Mr. Gupta?
options: Yes, because even a person with wrongful possession can bring an action against a trespasser.

No, because a person in wrongful possession cannot bring an action against the real owner of the
land.
Yes, because Mr. Gupta entered the property without Rohan's permission.
No, because Mr. Gupta did not cause any physical damage to the apartment.

questions.questionText:
Zoya held an indemnity for losses from a property deal. The seller won a court decree
        against her for ₹75 lakh. Zoya has not paid but demands the indemnifier pay the
        decree holder directly. The indemnifier refuses until she pays. What is Zoya's legal
        position?
options:
She must pay first, as liability commences only upon the actual disbursement of her
money.

She can sue for specific performance now; her liability is absolute under the decree,
triggering the indemnity.
She cannot claim yet as this is a guarantee, requiring her to sue the seller first.

She can only get a declaration of future liability; payment must precede any
reimbursement claim.

questions.questionText:
Judge Helen is presiding over a breach of contract case where the defendant is
       MegaCorp Inc. During a routine financial disclosure, it is revealed that Judge Helen
       owns 10 shares of MegaCorp stock, valued at approximately $150 in total. A party
       moves for her disqualification. What is the correct resolution?
options:
Judge Helen must recuse herself because she has a direct financial interest in a
               party.

Judge Helen can only be disqualified if the moving party provides direct
               evidence of her actual prejudice against them in this specific matter.

Judge Helen should seek the consent of both parties to continue, and if one
               objects, she must then step down from the proceedings entirely.

Judge Helen may continue to hear the case because her financial interest is de
               minimis and too trivial to affect her judgment or the public's perception.

questions.questionText:
Arjun discovered that a confidential report written by his former employer in 2020
       contained false statements that defamed him. He first saw this report in January 2024.
       Arjun filed a defamation lawsuit against the employer in March 2024.
options: The lawsuit is valid because the defamation was ongoing until he discovered it.

The lawsuit is barred by limitation as it was filed more than three years from the date
       the wrong was committed (2020).
The lawsuit is valid as the limitation period starts from the date of discovery (2024).

The lawsuit is barred because Arjun voluntarily assumed the risk of defamation by
       working there.

questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): Freedom of speech protects expressions that may offend or discomfort
       those in power.
Reason (R): Democratic culture requires tolerance of dissent rather than reflexive censorship.
Which option best reflects the relationship between A and R?
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.

questions.questionText:
A and C are business rivals. A provokes his close friend B by repeatedly telling him that C has
destroyed their future and deserves to be eliminated. Eventually, B—convinced by A's
provocation—stabs C with a knife in a public place. C survives after medical treatment. The
police arrest both A and B. What offence has A committed?
options: Not guilty since C didn’t die
Guilty of abetment of murder
Guilty only of attempt to murder
Guilty of abetment but with no punishment
questions.solution: Why (B) is correct: The passage explains under Section 109 that when the abetted act is committed, the abettor is liable as the principal offender. A repeatedly provoked B to eliminate C — this amounts to instigation under Section 107.

questions.questionText:
A prisoner files a habeas corpus petition challenging unlawful detention. The petition is
dismissed. Subsequently, fresh facts emerge showing a new detention order passed on
different grounds. The prisoner files another habeas corpus petition. Which of the following is
most consistent with the passage?
options: The second petition is automatically barred by constructive res judicata.

The second petition may be maintainable because courts recognize exceptions involving
changed circumstances and personal liberty.

The second petition is barred because all future challenges must be raised in the first
petition itself.
Constructive res judicata applies more strictly in matters involving liberty.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: The second petition may be maintainable because courts recognize exceptions involving changed circumstances and personal liberty. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): Courts must consider litigants’ vulnerabilities while adjudicating sexual offence
cases.
Reason (R): Justice cannot be complete if courts are inconsiderate to litigants’ vulnerabilities.
options: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
Ais true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.solution: Both statements are directly stated in the passage and the reason explains why courts must consider vulnerabilities — because ignoring them prevents complete justice. B is incorrect because the Reason directly explains the Assertion.

questions.questionText:
At a family function in Indore, Neel tells his cousin, “If you move to Jaipur for coaching, I'll pay
your rent for six months.” The cousin moves within a week and later asks for rent money. Neel
refuses, calling it a family assurance, not a binding deal. The cousin sues. Who is more likely to
succeed?
options:
The cousin, because acting on the assurance proves legal enforceability and removes any need
to show contractual intention.

Neel, because “Intention to create a legal relationship is an essential element,” and “social or
domestic arrangements do not” presume it.

The cousin, because shifting cities is sufficient consideration to prove the arrangement was
commercial-like and legally binding.

Neel, because paying rent can be enforced only if written on stamp paper and registered with
the local rent authority.
questions.solution: The reference line expressly states that “Intention to create a legal relationship is an essential element” and that “social or domestic arrangements do not” generally presume such intention. Because this promise was made at a family function and appears social in nature, Neel is more likely to succeed.

questions.questionText:
Mr. Ghosh, a Bengali by birth, follows the Brahmo faith. He dies intestate, leaving
       behind self-acquired property. His brother claims to be the legal heir under traditional
       Dayabhaga law. Under which statute will Mr. Ghosh's succession be governed?
options:
The Hindu Succession Act, 1956, applies as he was a Hindu by religion in one of its
      forms.

The traditional Dayabhaga school of law will apply exclusively, as it is a personal law
      for Bengali Hindus.

The Indian Succession Act, 1925, will apply because the Brahmo faith is considered a
      distinct religion.

The laws of intestate succession do not apply here as the property was self-acquired
      and not ancestral.

questions.questionText: D is nominated to the Rajya Sabha and takes oath on 1st January. On 15th July of the same year, D formally joins Party M, claiming that the delay was due to prolonged consultations and ideological alignment. A disqualification petition is filed. Which of the following is the most appropriate legal conclusion?
options: D is protected because nominated members enjoy complete discretion in choosing political affiliation at any time.
D is disqualified because nominated members can join a political party only within six months of taking their seat, and this period has expired.
D is protected because the decision was based on ideological considerations rather than political opportunism.
D is disqualified only if he votes against Party M's whip after joining it.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: D is disqualified because nominated members can join a political party only within six months of taking their seat, and this period has expired. Accordingly, option B is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
Based on the directives and observations in the passage, what can be inferred about the Court’s
philosophy on the eradication of the dowry system?
options:
The Court identifies judicial efficiency and the prompt incarceration of offenders as the most
vital mechanism to rectify the systemic bias that treats women as objects of financial
extraction.

The Court envisions eradication through a synthesis of specialized administrative enforcement
and a long-term recalibration of social values to align entrenched customs with constitutional
equality.

The Court’s strategy prioritizes the mandate of Article 14, implying that social practices must
be replaced by secular constitutional litigation to resolve the conflict between religious
protections and material demands.

The Court asserts that the "hollowing out" of protective customs like Mehrcan only be
corrected if the State assumes the role of regulating all forms of gift-giving between families.
questions.solution: Why B is correct- This option accurately synthesizes the Court’s two-fold strategy: institutional enforcement (empowering Prohibition Officers and sensitizing the judiciary) and structural social reform (reconditioning societal values through education). The judgment posits that while penal consequences are necessary, the ultimate eradication of dowry requires aligning entrenched customs with the constitutional mandate of equality.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Medical negligence law now focuses only on the individual doctor's fault.
Statement II: Systemic failures may be treated as violations of the right to treatment.
Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the statements?
options: Both statements are true, and Statement II explains Statement I
Both statements are false
Statement I is false, but Statement II is true
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false

questions.questionText:
A State government orders the removal of an online article criticising its economic
       policies, stating that the article may “cause dissatisfaction among citizens.” Based on
       the passage, which outcome is most consistent with constitutional principles?
options:
The removal is valid because governments may suppress speech that creates
       dissatisfaction.

The removal is invalid because mere discomfort or dissatisfaction does not justify
       restricting free speech.
The removal is valid because economic policy criticism affects public order.
The removal is valid unless the author proves the criticism is factually accurate.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court agreed with the High Court that the acts were merely preparatory.
2. The High Court reduced charges from rape/attempt to offences like Section 354-B IPC and
aggravated sexual assault.
8. The Supreme Court directed the National Judicial Academy to draft sensitivity guidelines.
4. The Supreme Court required guidelines to be written in simple, accessible language.
How many of the above are true?
options: Only one
Only two
Only three
All four
questions.solution: Statement 1 is false because the Supreme Court rejected the preparatory view. Statements 2, 3, and 4 are directly stated in the passage.

questions.questionText: T knew that his friend U planned to rob a jewellery store. T personally disagreed with the plan and repeatedly advised U not to proceed. However, when U later asked for directions to the store, T casually provided them without knowing whether U still intended to commit the offence. Which option is most appropriate?
options: T automatically committed aiding because any information given to an offender amounts to assistance.
T committed conspiracy because he knew of U's intentions.
T may not be liable because intentional assistance appears absent.
T committed instigation because he interacted with U before the offence.
questions.solution: Applying the rule stated in the passage to the facts in the question leads to this conclusion: T may not be liable because intentional assistance appears absent. Accordingly, option C is the keyed legal result.

questions.questionText:
The President of India issues an Ordinance (a legislative act) during a time when Parliament is
not in session. A citizen challenges this, arguing it violates the separation of powers as only the
Legislature should make laws. Based on the passage, will this challenge succeed?
options: No, because the Indian framework does not imply a rigid separation
Yes, because the Functional Principle prevents one organ from performing tasks
Yes, because the Exclusivity Principle mandates a strict division of organs
No, because the President is part of the Judiciary in India
questions.solution: , as the passage clarifies that the doctrine is not applied with "pedantic rigor" and allows for certain overlaps like the President's legislative powers.

questions.questionText:
While driving to work, Priya was texting on her phone and failed to notice a stop sign.
       At the same intersection, Dev, also driving, was exceeding the speed limit. Their cars
       collided. Priya suffers injuries and sues Dev for damages.
options: Dev is fully liable because Priya's actions were a minor contributing factor.

Priya cannot recover any damages because her contributory negligence completely
       bars her claim.
Liability will be apportioned between both parties based on their share of fault.

questions.questionText:
Based on the passage, what can be inferred about the Supreme Court’s use of Article 142 in the
April 2025 judgment?
options: It is a standard procedure used to set permanent timelines for all constitutional authorities.

It was used as an extraordinary measure to provide complete justice in case of unreasonable
delay.

questions.solution: The passage mentions the Court used Article 142 in the "exceptional facts of the case."
